keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 306 shape (565,000 km2, 103.6-115.0 E, 34.3-40.9 N: the whole of Shanxi and the Ordos side) is far larger than anything the page records before 308: capitals Lishi (304-305), Liting (305-308), Puzi (308-309), then Pingyang after 'the Han conquered Pingyang commandery' in 308. The 100 km disc around Lishi is the page's own seat; the rest of the shape is unverified beyond the page's statement that at its height the state ruled Shanxi. Cliopatria starts in 306, the page's 'Established: late 304'.

keyframe_review.note: 311-323. The shape (647,071 km2 in the table, 794,000 km2 by the gazetteer's cells) holds Shaanxi, Shanxi, Henan, the Ordos and Ningxia. Page checks: 311 Luoyang and Emperor Huai captured; 312 'Emperor Min [was installed] at Chang'an'; 316 Chang'an falls. The infobox gives 'Area: 2,000,000 km2 in 316', ratio 0.32 against the table. The page's own list of provinces (Shanxi, Shaanxi, eastern Gansu, 'large parts of Shandong, Hebei, and Henan') is smaller than that figure (all of Shanxi, Shaanxi, Shandong, Hebei and Henan together are about 1.1 M km2 by the gazetteer's cells, and the Han held 'large parts' of three of them), so the infobox figure is taken as inflated and the shape stands apart from Guanzhong. Unverified: the Ordos, Ningxia and eastern Gansu part (Liu Yao 'later defeated the Di and Qiang rebellion', undated; Former Liang submitted in 323). fx-29 (F249): the Dai core is cut (256 cells of the shape: 158 Shanxi, 65 Inner Mongolia, 33 Hebei). Dai page: Tuoba Yilu was made Duke of Dai by Western Jin in 310 'as a reward for helping Liu Kun' against Han-Zhao and forced Liu Kun to give him 'five counties north of the mountain ranges'; the Tuoba stayed 'a vital fighting force for Jin in their war against Han'; capital Shengle 310-324. The Han-Zhao page, which says the Han 'ruled Shanxi' at its height, does not name Dai, the Tuoba or Inner Mongolia.

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria draws the Former Zhao to 336 although the page says 'Disestablished: 329' (Liu Yao captured on 21 January 329; Liu Xi killed at Shanggui in the same year). 330-336 are Later Zhao's land; Cliopatria's Later Zhao row begins only in 337. 647,071 km2. fx-29 (F249): the Dai core is cut as in the 311 keyframe (Dai page: Heru moved the capital to Mount Dongmugen in 324 and Lady Qi 'submitted to the Later Zhao dynasty').

region.text: Lishi, the seat of the Southern Xiongnu's Five Divisions

ledger.note: 304: Liu Yuan founds the Han at Lishi. 'Liu Yuan declared himself Grand Chanyu at Lishi, then proclaimed himself "King of Han" later that year'; infobox 'Established: late 304'.

region.text: Pingyang Commandery, the Fen valley round Linfen

ledger.note: 308: Pingyang falls to the Han. 'In 308, the Han conquered Pingyang commandery and moved the capital to Puzi' (then to Pingyang city in 309); Liu Yuan took the imperial title on 2 November 308.
308: the capital moves to Puzi (infobox: Puzi 308-309, Pingyang 309-318, after Lishi and Liting).

region.text: Luoyang and the Henan plain round it, after the Disaster of Yongjia

ledger.note: 311: Luoyang falls. 'Shi Le destroyed the Jin imperial army at the Battle of Ningping. Han forces then captured Luoyang and Emperor Huai in the Disaster of Yongjia.'

region.text: Chang'an and the Wei valley: 'Liu Yao captured Chang'an, ending the Western Jin dynasty and taking Emperor Min'

ledger.note: 316: Chang'an falls and the Western Jin ends. Emperor Min, installed at Chang'an in 312, is taken.
318: Liu Yao, acclaimed emperor after Jin Zhun's failed coup, moves the capital to Chang'an (infobox: Chang'an 318-329).

region.text: Shi Le's lands: Liu Yao 'executed Shi Le's envoy, prompting Shi Le to declare independence'; 'large parts of Shandong, Hebei, and Henan' ruled at the height

ledger.note: 319: Shi Le breaks away. Liu Yao executes his envoy and Shi Le declares independence; in 319 he names his state Zhao, the Later Zhao. The page gives no boundary for Shi Le's lands; Cliopatria's Former Zhao shape holds little of Hebei and Shandong, so the event moves little drawn land. [Reviewer ea-03-b: year 318 corrected to 319; the Han-Zhao page has 'the Later Zhao founded by Shi Le in 319'.]
319: Liu Yao renames the state Zhao. 'Liu Yao renamed the state Zhao'; Shi Le then calls his own state Zhao: the Former and Later Zhao.

region.text: Liang Province under Zhang Mao, who 'submitted to the Former Zhao, receiving the title of King of Liang'

ledger.note: 323: Zhang Mao of Liang submits. 'Submitted to Former Zhao and received the title of King of Liang. He kept his Jin title of Duke of Xiping internally.' The Han-Zhao page adds that Liu Yao 'forced the Former Liang into submission' and invaded Chouchi 'by 323'.

region.text: Henan and Luoyang, where the two Zhao states fought until 329

ledger.note: 324: war between the two Zhao states. 'War between the two Zhao states broke out' (324); the page names Henan (328) and Luoyang (328-329) as the ground.

region.text: the lands south of the Yellow River in Liang Province, taken by Liu Yin in 327 and recovered by Former Liang in 329

ledger.note: 327: Liu Yin counterattacks in Liang. After Zhang Jun 'attacks Former Zhao's Qin Province, Liu Yin counterattacks and takes Former Liang territory south of the Yellow River.'

region.text: Henan, which Liu Yao 'secured ... from Later Zhao'

ledger.note: 328: Liu Yao takes Henan from Later Zhao, before the Battle of Luoyang. The page says only that 'in 328, Liu Yao led his forces to secure the Henan region from Later Zhao' and that the two sides 'came head to head at the Battle of Luoyang'. [Reviewer ea-03-b: confidence 3 lowered to 2; the page gives the aim, not the land taken.]

region.text: Liang Province after the fall of the Former Zhao

ledger.note: 329: the Former Zhao falls; Liang's submission passes to the victor. 'After Later Zhao conquered Former Zhao in 329, [Zhang Jun] first rejected Later Zhao's authority, then was pressured into submission' (Former Liang page).

region.text: the lands south of the Yellow River in Liang Province, taken by Liu Yin in 327 and recovered by Former Liang in 329

ledger.note: 329: Former Liang recovers the lands south of the Yellow River as the Former Zhao falls: 'Former Zhao falls to Later Zhao, and Former Liang recovers the lands south of the Yellow River.'

329: Liu Yao is captured at Luoyang on 21 January. 'Liu Yao was captured by Later Zhao soldiers during the Battle of Luoyang and was executed' (infobox: 21 January 329; the event carries no month so that it sorts before the same-year dissolve, whose month the page does not give).

region.text: the Han-Zhao realm: Chang'an, Shanggui and the Shanxi and Henan lands

ledger.note: 329: the Former Zhao ends. 'Liu Xi was driven from the capital and killed at Shanggui by Later Zhao forces, ending the state.'

wars.name: Former Liang-Former Zhao war for the Yellow River lands

zones.text: the lands south of the Yellow River in Liang Province, taken by Liu Yin in 327 and recovered by Former Liang in 329

wars.outcome: Liu Yin took Former Liang land south of the Yellow River in 327; it returned to Former Liang in 329 when Former Zhao fell.

wars.name: Han-Zhao conquest of the Western Jin
wars.outcome: The Han take Pingyang (308), Luoyang and Emperor Huai (311, Disaster of Yongjia) and Chang'an and Emperor Min (316), ending the Western Jin.
wars.note: Shi Le, later the founder of Later Zhao, commanded at the Battle of Ningping (311).

wars.name: Zhao campaign against the Di, Qiang and Former Liang
wars.outcome: Liu Yao defeated the Di and Qiang rebels, moved nearly 200,000 people to Chang'an, and made Zhang Mao of Former Liang a vassal in 323.
wars.note: The Han-Zhao page does not date the Di and Qiang rebellion; 'by 323' for the Chouchi invasion; the 320 start is Zhang Mao's accession, when he 'came into conflict with Former Zhao' (Former Liang page), so the span 320-323 is the researcher's reading.

wars.name: War between the Former and Later Zhao
wars.outcome: Liu Yao secured Henan in 328; at the Battle of Luoyang (328-329) he was captured on 21 January 329; Liu Xi was killed at Shanggui and the Former Zhao ended.

certainty.note: Commandery frontiers in Shanxi and Shaanxi; the Ordos and eastern Gansu edge and the Henan front are approximate; no page opened gives a treaty or survey line.

notes:
Cliopatria rows: 'Former Zhao', 3 shapes, 306..336, all reviewed. Wikidata Q1574107 is shared with 'zhao' (the Warring States Zhao, -404..-226): these are two different states, 600 years apart; Cliopatria's Wikidata link is a mistake and Q1574107 is kept in identity only because it is Cliopatria's value. No Wikidata item for Han-Zhao was available to me (wikidata.org is unreachable).
Cliopatria errors: (1) the 306 shape is far too large for 304-307; (2) the 311 shape includes Guanzhong, which Jin held until 316; (3) the shapes run to 336 although the state ended in 329, and Later Zhao is missing from 330 to 336; (4) the infobox area (2.0 M km2, 316) cannot be reconciled with the page's provinces and is treated as inflated.
Unsettled: the Di and Qiang rebellion (undated); where exactly Liting was (coordinates are a placement); the Henan front between Former Zhao and Shi Le from 319 to 328 (the page dates only 324, 328 and 328-329); whether Hebei and Shandong were Han land before 318 (the page names them for the height of the state only).
Gazetteer names needed: Lishi (Lüliang, Shanxi; used as a lon/lat disc), Liting, Puzi, Shanggui (Tianshui) as place names; none of them resolves in places.jsonl.
Counterparts needing dossiers: later-zhao (mine), former-liang (mine), Chouchi (a Xiongnu-Di state; no group named); 'Di and Qiang rebels' are not a state.
